text: So, let's look back at the loop.
The Indus cities stitched together, shone and went silent.
The Marias stitched the land together, shone and shattered.
Then the Guptas, then the Sultans, then the Mughals.
Every time outsiders marched in, and every time, India absorbed them.
Their food, their words, their buildings, their gods, all became part of the same story.
Winding his watch, stitch, shine, shatter, absorb.
Three hundred years ago, India made about a quarter of everything in the world.
Fast. The question is no longer whether the golden bird can fly again. It's whether this
time India can shine without the shatter.
Looking up, I've seen how this story usually goes. But I've also seen this land surprise
everyone. Many times. What do you think? Can India break the loop?
